analysis.title: Marketcolour + Mutual Fund / HF Update / Europe HC / VAR (dg) / Schindler / FLSmidth / Rational
key_insights: US equities fell for a 6th straight session (about 6% over the stretch). SPX -202bps to 7175 with 11 of 11 sectors down and VIX +16% to 28.47. NDX -221bps to 26517 (now +5% YTD). RTY -218bps to 2655.
The AI trade reversed early strength and closed lower. GS AI Semis basket (GSBSMHX) -2.91% and GS Data Center basket (GSTMTDAT) -2.29%.

Industrials is the second most net sold US sector MTD behind Info Tech, where net exposure is at its lowest in more than two years. Consumer Staples is also among the most net sold sectors MTD, which suggests managers have been fading the sector's price rally.
Asset managers and hedge funds net sold macro products and net bought pockets of consumer and financials. No sector screened materially for sale.
Liquidity is poor and is exacerbating price action. S&P top of book averages just $4mm on the touch.
42% of large-cap mutual funds are beating their benchmarks YTD versus a historical average of 37%. High return dispersion and better market breadth have supported fund returns.

Mutual funds were underweight AI-exposed equities ahead of the recent weakness in the AI complex. Large-cap funds were 722 bp underweight the Mag 7 at end of Q3 2026, effectively unchanged on the quarter.
Large-cap mutual funds are most overweight Industrials (+200 bp), Health Care (+199 bp, a 10-year high) and Financials (+196 bp). Basket: GSTHMFOW.

Global Fundamental L/S managers are -0.2% in November (+8.9% YTD as of Nov 16), with beta losses partly offset by positive alpha from short-side gains. Hedge funds heavily net sold global equities in November, with long and short sales at roughly 3 to 1.
Single stocks were net sold in 7 of the last 8 weeks. Fundamental L/S net leverage fell a further 7.6 pts MTD to its lowest in more than five years, now below the Liberation Day lows.
CTA: broader market weakness was potentially driven by systematic flow while liquidity is low. The weakness was exacerbated at the US open and caused many names to erase earlier gains.

Europe healthcare: Buy reiterated on AstraZeneca (growth and pipeline optionality, increasingly attractive valuation), Bayer (underappreciated Pharma business, asymmetric risk/reward), and Argenx (on CL), Galderma and UCB (outsized revenue growth supporting premium valuations).
Novartis stays Sell. Patent expirations are expected to keep weighing on earnings momentum, downside risks are not adequately reflected, and the stock trades at a premium to the sector.

Vår Energy cut to Neutral. New gas assumptions lower the 12m price target to NOK51 from NOK70 (c.7% upside). GS still likes its exploration success and short-cycle production delivery but sees longer-term downside risk to TTF prices, with upside risk to TTF this winter.

Schindler (Sell, PT CHF250, 15% downside): the market reacted cautiously to the lack of precise quantitative margin guidance and no increase in cash returned to shareholders. Consensus is already close to best-in-class margins, and the stock is up 20% in L3M versus the sector down 2%.
FLSmidth: Buy reiterated, described as now a contrarian stance. Feedback after the CMD targets and CFO change has been cautious, which is arguably reflected in the stock's 20% fall.

Rational (Buy, PT EUR833, 35% upside): CMD takeaways show limited direct monetization mid-term and no new changes to the financial outlook. GS sees the CMD as strengthening the company's moat versus peers and improving customer benefits.
